title: Weil transport on finite etale fibres before passage to torsors
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{k}_0$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $U_0$ be a geometrically connected separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$, and choose a geometric point $\bar u\to U$. Write $F=F_{\bar u}:\mathrm{F\acute Et}(U)\to\mathbf{FinSets}$ and $\Pi=\operatorname{Aut}(F)=\pi_1(U,\bar u)$, with the categories and topology of [def-galois-categories] and [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Let $W=W(U_0,\bar u)$ with its degree map be as in [def-wf-weil-group], and regard $\Pi$ as its geometric subgroup. Write $\Phi_U=\operatorname{id}_{U_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, where $\gamma:z\mapsto z^{1/q}$ is geometric Frobenius on $k$, with the convention of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed].

For $s\in W$ and $n=\deg(s)\in\mathbf Z$, define the covariant transport $T_n$ of finite etale covers by
$$
T_n(P\xrightarrow{p}U)=(P\xrightarrow{\Phi_U^n\circ p}U)
$$
and by leaving the underlying maps of covers unchanged. There exists an isomorphism of finite-set-valued functors $\tau_s:F\circ T_n\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ for which
$$
\tau_{s,P}(g\cdot x)=(sgs^{-1})\cdot\tau_{s,P}(x)
\quad(P\in\mathrm{F\acute Et}(U),\ g\in\Pi,\ x\in F(T_nP)).
$$
Equivalently, using $T_{-n}\cong(\Phi_U^n)^*$, there is a natural fibre bijection
$$
\lambda_{s,P}:F((\Phi_U^n)^*P)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(P),\qquad
\lambda_{s,P}(g\cdot x)=(s^{-1}gs)\cdot\lambda_{s,P}(x).
$$
Naturality here is with respect to every morphism of finite etale $U$-schemes, not only isomorphisms. No group action on $P$, coefficient group, or cohomology group is assumed.

proof.text: Put $\phi=\Phi_U$ and write $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, with scalar embedding $\iota:k\hookrightarrow\Omega$. By [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $\phi$ is an automorphism. For every integer $r$, the projection to $P$ identifies $(\phi^{-r})^*P$ with $T_rP$: its inverse sends $z$ to $(z,\phi^r p(z))$. These two maps are inverse by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] and commute with every cover morphism. Pullback gives a finite-etale cover by [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], so $T_r$ is a well-defined functor, with inverse $T_{-r}$.

proof.text: Let $u_0$ be the composite of $\bar u$ with $U\to U_0$, put $F_0=F_{u_0}$ and $A=\operatorname{Aut}(F_0)$. The canonical map $i:\Pi\to A$ and the natural fibre identifications for base change are [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality]. The identification of $\Pi$ with the geometric subgroup of $W\subseteq A$, including its normality, is [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence]. We use $i$ for this inclusion throughout. The degree convention [def-wf-weil-group] says that an element of degree $d$ acts on the fibre of the constant cover $U_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}E$, for every finite subextension $E\subseteq k$, by $\iota\sigma\mapsto\iota\gamma^d\sigma$ on $k_0$-embeddings $E\hookrightarrow k$. This is simply the restriction of its image $\gamma^d\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, with the geometric convention of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed].

proof.text: Every finite subextension $E/k_0$ of $k$ is a finite field, hence separable and normal by [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius]. Since every element of the algebraic closure lies in a finite subextension, $k/k_0$ is separable algebraic. Apply [lem-wf-finite-etale-field-limit-descent](1) to $U_0$ and $k/k_0$: choose a finite $E$ and $P_E\to U_E=U_0\times_{k_0}E$ with $P\cong P_E\times_E k$. Regard $Q=P_E$ as a cover of $U_0$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is finite by finite-dimensionality and etale by [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion]. Its base change $U_E\to U_0$ is finite etale by [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Thus $Q\to U_0$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. This puts $Q$ in the domain of $F_0$, without assuming that $P$ has a group action.

proof.text: For $r\in\mathbf Z$, let $S_r(Q)\subseteq F_0(Q)$ consist of those points whose restriction to $E$ is $\iota\gamma^{-r}|_E$. Projection $P=P_E\times_E k\to P_E=Q$ gives a bijection $j_r:F(T_rP)\to S_r(Q)$. Indeed a point $x$ of $T_rP$ satisfies $p x=\phi^{-r}\bar u$, so its scalar map on $k$ is $\iota\gamma^{-r}$. Conversely, a point $y$ of $Q$ with the indicated restriction on $E$, together with the scalar map $\iota\gamma^{-r}:k\to\Omega$, gives a unique point of $P_E\times_E k$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]; its projections to $U_0$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are those of $\phi^{-r}\bar u$, so it belongs to $F(T_rP)$. The two constructions are inverse. The isomorphism chosen in step 3 is inserted in these formulas when $P$ is not literally this fibre product.

proof.text:
Use the arithmetic cover morphism $Q\to U_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}E$ induced by its $U_0$- and $E$-maps. Naturality of $s\in\operatorname{Aut}(F_0)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor] and its degree-$n$ action on the latter cover [def-wf-weil-group] show that $s$ carries $S_n(Q)$ bijectively to $S_0(Q)$: on restrictions to $E$ the formula is $\iota\gamma^{-n}\mapsto\iota\gamma^n\gamma^{-n}=\iota$. The inverse is the action of $s^{-1}$. Define
$$\tau_{s,P}=j_0^{-1}\circ s_Q\circ j_n.$$
Its inverse is $j_n^{-1}\circ(s^{-1})_Q\circ j_0$, so it is a finite-set bijection.

proof.text: The bijection is independent of the finite-stage model. For a refinement $E\subseteq E'$, the projection $P_E\times_E E'\to P_E$ is a morphism of arithmetic covers. On fibres it commutes with $j_r$ for every $r$, because both composites are the same projection of the point of $P$; the scalar restrictions are $\iota\gamma^{-r}|_{E'}$ and $\iota\gamma^{-r}|_E$. It also commutes with $s$, since $s$ is a natural automorphism [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Hence both definitions of $\tau_{s,P}$ have the same image under the injective map $j_0$ for the smaller model, and agree. For two arbitrary models, take a common finite overfield, descend the comparison isomorphism and its inverse using [lem-wf-finite-etale-field-limit-descent](2), and enlarge once more so that both inverse identities hold by (3). The preceding projection calculation and naturality of $s$ with respect to this descended isomorphism identify the two answers.

proof.text:
Let $f:P\to P'$ be any morphism in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(U)$. Choose models at a common finite stage and descend $f$ by [lem-wf-finite-etale-field-limit-descent](2). The resulting $f_E:P_E\to P'_E$ is a morphism of arithmetic covers. Write $b=F_0(f_E)$. Projection of points gives $j'_r F(T_rf)=b j_r$ for $r=0,n$; naturality of $s$ gives $b s_Q=s_{Q'}b$ [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Consequently
$$j'_0 F(f)\tau_{s,P}=b s_Qj_n=s_{Q'}b j_n=j'_0\tau_{s,P'}F(T_nf).$$
Cancel the injection $j'_0$. Model independence from step 6 makes this equality valid for the chosen bijections on all objects simultaneously. Thus $\tau_s:F\circ T_n\cong F$ is natural for every morphism, with no isomorphism assumption on $f$.

source.place: Tags 0BN5 (lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), 0BTV (lemma-limit), 0BTX (lemma-ses-field); explicit agent-written finite-stage argument for the penultimate paragraph of lem-wf-finite-constant-h1-pi1.proof.md in main-20261015.

proof.text:
For each $r$, the pair of maps $P\to Q$ and $\phi^r p:P\to U$ gives a $U$-morphism $v_r:T_rP\to Q\times_{U_0}U$ by [def-pc-fibre-product], since $\phi$ lies over $U_0$. Under the natural fibre identification $F(Q\times_{U_0}U)\cong F_0(Q)$ of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], $F(v_r)$ is exactly $j_r$. Naturality of $g\in\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor] and that fibre identification give
$$j_r(gx)=i(g)j_r(x).$$
Normality and the identification of the geometric subgroup in [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence] give $s i(g)s^{-1}=i(sgs^{-1})$. Therefore
$$j_0\tau_{s,P}(gx)=s i(g)j_n(x)=i(sgs^{-1})s j_n(x)=j_0((sgs^{-1})\tau_{s,P}(x)).$$
Cancel $j_0$ to obtain precisely the first required formula.

source.place: Tags 0BN5 (lemma-functoriality-galois), 0BND (theorem-fundamental-group), 0BTV (lemma-limit), 0BTX (lemma-ses-field); explicit agent-written finite-stage argument for the penultimate paragraph of lem-wf-finite-constant-h1-pi1.proof.md in main-20261015.

proof.text:
Apply the established construction to $s^{-1}$, whose degree is $-n$ by [def-wf-weil-group]. Step 1 with $r=-n$ gives the natural comparison $(\phi^n)^*P\cong T_{-n}P$, explicitly the projection to $P$ with inverse $z\mapsto(z,\phi^{-n}p(z))$. Set $\lambda_{s,P}$ equal to its fibre map followed by $\tau_{s^{-1},P}$. Every natural map of covers induces a map commuting with $g\in\Pi$ by [def-galois-fibre-functor], so step 8 for $s^{-1}$ gives
$$\lambda_{s,P}(gx)=(s^{-1}gs)\lambda_{s,P}(x).$$
The same construction with $s^{-1}$ recovers the covariant formulation from the pullback formulation. This proves the stated equivalence and all naturality assertions.

lean.statement: theorem finiteEtaleWeilTransport (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (U₀ : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k₀))) [GeometricallyConnected U₀.hom] [IsSeparated U₀.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType U₀.hom] [QuasiCompact U₀.hom] {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ (D.geometricFiber U₀).left) (w : weilGroup U₀.hom (s ≫ Limits.pullback.fst U₀.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap D.k₀ D.k)))) (Aut (fiber (s ≫ Limits.pullback.fst U₀.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap D.k₀ D.k))))))) : (∃ τ : covariantTransport ((D.geometricFrobenius U₀) ^ w.val.2.toAdd) ⋙ fiber s ≅ fiber s, ∀ g : Aut (fiber s), ∃! h : Aut (fiber s), fiberAutBaseChange (Limits.pullback.fst U₀.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap D.k₀ D.k)))) s h = w.val.1 * fiberAutBaseChange (Limits.pullback.fst U₀.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap D.k₀ D.k)))) s g * w.val.1⁻¹ ∧ ∀ (P : (D.geometricFiber U₀).left.FiniteEtale) (x : (fiber s).obj ((covariantTransport ((D.geometricFrobenius U₀) ^ w.val.2.toAdd)).obj P)), τ.hom.app P (g.hom.app _ x) = h.hom.app P (τ.hom.app P x)) ∧ Nonempty (covariantTransport ((D.geometricFrobenius U₀) ^ (-w.val.2.toAdd)) ≅ pullback ((D.geometricFrobenius U₀) ^ w.val.2.toAdd).hom) ∧ (∃ lam : pullback ((D.geometricFrobenius U₀) ^ w.val.2.toAdd).hom ⋙ fiber s ≅ fiber s, ∀ g : Aut (fiber s), ∃! h : Aut (fiber s), fiberAutBaseChange (Limits.pullback.fst U₀.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap D.k₀ D.k)))) s h = w.val.1⁻¹ * fiberAutBaseChange (Limits.pullback.fst U₀.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap D.k₀ D.k)))) s g * w.val.1 ∧ ∀ (P : (D.geometricFiber U₀).left.FiniteEtale) (x : (fiber s).obj ((pullback ((D.geometricFrobenius U₀) ^ w.val.2.toAdd).hom).obj P)), lam.hom.app P (g.hom.app _ x) = h.hom.app P (lam.hom.app P x))
lean.note: States both finite-cover transport formulations for the actual Aut(fiber) groups. The two helper definitions construct postcomposition transport and the canonical base-change map on natural automorphisms from existing functors; neither uses postponed data. Conjugates are expressed by their unique geometric preimages under this canonical map. The integer w.val.2.toAdd is definitionally weilGroupDeg applied to w.
